newsitem.title: USA: Rain aids Illinois crops, corn harvest begins.
newsitem.headline: Rain aids Illinois crops, corn harvest begins.

text.p: Scattered rain during the week ended Sunday aided Illinois corn and soybeans as did the warm weather, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
More warm weather was needed to promote crop progress in the northern districts, while limited corn harvest began in the southern areas.

About three percent of the corn was mature versus five a year ago and the 16 percent average. About 36 had dented versus 57 a year ago and the 61 average. The crop was rated 52 percent good to excellent, unchanged from a week ago. Thirty-one percent was fair, 12 poor and five very poor.
Soybeans were rated 41 percent good to excellent, 37 fair, 12 poor and five very poor. Less than one percent was shedding leaves versus one a year ago and the seven average.
Sorghum was 26 percent coloring versus 12 a year ago and the 45 average.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent surplus, 46 adequate, 36 short and 17 very short.
